title: Threadress Origin Story
text: Threadress emerged from personal struggle to find specific items - spending hours searching helplessly only to discover nothing remotely similar. Despite recent developments, search engines like Google still prioritize sponsored brands and items over genuinely tailored fashion recommendations based on user intent. We're committed to changing this paradigm. With the emergence of powerful AI tools, we successfully built our first MVP and are now focused on scaling our impact. Co-founder Clara and I have been discussing building something together since freshman year, but it wasn't until junior year that we actually began development, after establishing the necessary connections and securing the right resources.

title: Threadress Problem & Solution
text: Problem: Clara and I would spend hours searching for specific fashion items online, only to find nothing remotely similar. Search engines prioritize sponsored brands over genuinely tailored fashion recommendations. Solution: We recognized that with powerful AI tools, we could build a solution that truly understands shopper intent. We started by conducting discovery with 50+ NYC boutiques to understand their pain points - they had beautiful inventory but struggled with discoverability. Technical decision: We chose multimodal embeddings and vector retrieval because we needed to translate natural language queries (like 'flowy summer dress with floral pattern') into actual in-stock products. This required understanding both text descriptions and visual features of garments.

title: Threadress Technical Challenges
text: The biggest challenge was integrating with different POS systems. We discovered that boutiques use either Square or Shopify, and each has different APIs and data structures. We had to design our system to be flexible enough to handle both. Current focus: We're now prototyping a virtual try-on system using MediaPipe because we realized that seeing how a piece looks on your body is crucial for boutique shopping. This is especially important since shoppers can't physically try on items before purchasing. Learning: Building Threadress taught me that the best products emerge from deeply understanding both sides of a marketplace - the shoppers' frustrations and the retailers' operational constraints.

title: NEXUS Hackathon Project
text: Problem: Financial markets are complex - macro events (like Fed rate changes) have cascading effects across sectors, but most analysis tools are either too high-level or too granular. Solution: Built NEXUS as a multi-agent system where different AI agents specialize in different aspects: one detects macro events, another analyzes sector impacts, and another provides micro-level stock recommendations. Technical choice: Chose n8n for orchestration because we needed to connect multiple LLM agents and MCP (Model Context Protocol) tools. The visual workflow made it easier to iterate during the hackathon. Winning factor: The judges were impressed by our end-to-end design - we didn't just build a prototype, we thought through the entire user experience from event detection to actionable insights. Learning: This project showed the power of agentic AI systems. Instead of one large model trying to do everything, specialized agents working together can produce better results.

title: What Problem Threadress Solves
text: Threadress connects shoppers with real-time boutique inventory. When you search for 'flowy summer dress with floral pattern,' we use AI to understand your intent and show you actual in-stock items from local boutiques. We're bridging the gap between online search and in-store retail, helping boutiques get discovered while helping shoppers find exactly what they're looking for.

title: How Threadress Product-Matching Engine Works
text: We use multimodal embeddings to understand both text descriptions and visual features of garments. When a shopper searches, we convert their query into a vector embedding. We then search our vector database of boutique inventory to find the closest matches. This allows us to understand semantic meaning - 'flowy' and 'airy' are similar concepts, even if the exact words don't match.

text: The biggest learning is that the best products emerge from deeply understanding both sides of a marketplace. title: Fashion Tech - Digital Fashion Trends
text: Digital fashion is becoming a real economy. People are spending real money on virtual garments for their avatars. This isn't just a gaming trend - it's about self-expression and identity in digital spaces. Brands that ignore this are missing a huge opportunity, especially with Gen Z and Gen Alpha who are native to these platforms.

title: Fashion Tech - Sustainability
text: Digital fashion has massive environmental benefits - 97% less waste compared to physical production. But we need to be honest about AI's carbon footprint. Training models and running inference still has environmental costs. The industry needs better tools to measure and reduce this impact.

title: Fashion Tech - Avatar Economies
text: Each platform (Roblox, Snapchat, Zepeto, Bitmoji) has a unique fashion culture. Roblox is more gaming-focused, while Bitmoji is about personal expression. Brands need to understand these nuances to succeed. A one-size-fits-all approach won't work.

title: Retail Tech - Boutique Discovery
text: Small boutiques have beautiful, unique inventory but struggle with discoverability. They can't compete with large retailers on SEO or advertising spend. AI-powered search that understands intent can level the playing field, helping shoppers find exactly what they want while helping boutiques get discovered.

title: Retail Tech - Real-Time Inventory
text: The future of retail is real-time inventory visibility. Shoppers want to know what's actually available, not what might be in stock. This requires deep POS integration and real-time data sync, which is technically challenging but essential for trust.

title: Retail Tech - Virtual Try-On
text: Virtual try-on is becoming table stakes for online fashion. But current solutions are mostly for large retailers. We need tools that work for smaller boutiques too, using accessible technology like MediaPipe rather than expensive 3D scanning systems.

title: AI/ML - Multimodal AI
text: The future of search is multimodal. Text-only search is limiting - fashion is visual. Multimodal embeddings that understand both text and images will transform how people discover products. This is especially powerful for fashion where style, color, and silhouette matter more than keywords.

title: AI/ML - Agentic Systems
text: Multi-agent AI systems are more powerful than single large models. Specialized agents working together can produce better results - one agent detects events, another analyzes impacts, another provides recommendations. This is the architecture we used for NEXUS and it's the future of complex AI applications.

title: AI/ML - Vector Databases
text: Vector databases are essential for semantic search. Traditional keyword search can't understand intent - 'flowy dress' and 'airy garment' should return similar results. Vector embeddings capture semantic meaning, making search much more intelligent.

title: AI/ML - LLM Agents
text: LLM agents are becoming more practical with tools like n8n for orchestration and MCP (Model Context Protocol) for connecting different services. This makes it easier to build complex AI systems without being an ML engineer.

title: Product Management - User Research
text: The best products come from deep user research. For Threadress, talked to 50+ boutiques before building anything. This discovery process shaped entire product strategy. You can't build a good product without understanding your users' actual problems and constraints.

title: Product Management - Technical PM
text: Technical PMs who can code are becoming more valuable. You don't need to be a software engineer, but understanding how things are built helps you make better decisions, communicate with engineers, and build better products. Technical skills have been crucial for Threadress.

title: Product Management - Marketplace Dynamics
text: Building a marketplace requires understanding both sides. You can't optimize for one side at the expense of the other. For Threadress, we need to help shoppers find what they want AND help boutiques get discovered and make sales. This balance is critical.
